links.outcome: Readability grade level of AI-rewritten vs original pediatric orthopaedic patient education materials
links.effect: English Flesch-Kincaid grade 9.8 to 5.8 (P<.001); Flesch Reading Ease 56.9 to 76.4; Spanish Fernández Huerta 81.0 to 100.7 (P<.001). 10 reviewed PEMs judged accurate.
links.quote: The AI model was able to significantly improve the readability of the PEMs in every formula used (Flesch Reading Ease: 76.4 vs 56.9, P < .0001; Flesch-Kincaid grade level: 5.8 vs 9.8, P < .0001; SMOG Index: 8.7 vs 11.8, P < .0001; Coleman Liau: 8.7 vs 11.6, P < .0001; Automated Readability Score: 7.8 vs 12.0, P < .0001; Dale-Chall Readability Score: 7.8 vs 8.8, P < .0001; Linsear Write Formula: 6.6 vs 10.7, P = <.0001; Gunning Fog: 7.1 vs 10.8, P < .0001).

links.outcome: Reading grade level of patient materials after AI rewriting to fifth-sixth grade target
links.effect: Mean English grade level fell from 9.8 to 5.8 (P<.001), meeting the NIH/AMA target; Spanish materials moved from fifth-sixth to fourth grade.
links.quote: The average Flesch-Kincaid score of our AI-modified PEMs was 5.8 which corresponds to a sixth-grade reading level, meeting the standard set by the NIH.

links.outcome: Reading level of existing AAOS English pediatric orthopaedic patient materials
links.effect: Existing AAOS English PEMs averaged about 9.8 grade level (Flesch-Kincaid), above the fifth-sixth grade recommendation.
links.quote: Our study demonstrates that in the field of pediatric orthopaedics, the current PEMs published by the AAOS in English language are geared, on average, to a 10th-grade reading level.

links.outcome: Clinician-assessed accuracy of AI-rewritten patient materials against source OrthoInfo PEMs
links.effect: A single pediatric orthopaedic surgeon found all 10 reviewed AI-generated English PEMs accurate, with no confabulation identified.
links.quote: A single pediatric orthopaedic surgeon read and validated 10 AI model–generated PEMs and found them all to be accurate.
